the_claim_under_test: 'after he does them at least once, he would learn all of those permanently' -- so: does the second call RECALL the command, or does it secretly search again?
answer_before_this_round: it secretly searched again. Every surface said otherwise.

1_recall_verified_without_the_goal.why_fatal: every .txt plan was checked by carries_content_evidence, which is hard-False for .txt and must stay so
1_recall_verified_without_the_goal.measured: a goal that closed in 1.27 s was re-found in 0.10 s by searching again; from_memory was always False

2_verification_replayed_on_the_wrong_inp.why_fatal: the plan was replayed against the default one-line sandbox file and then compared to the caller's real 7-line input, so it could never match
2_verification_replayed_on_the_wrong_inp.measured: fingerprint similarity was 1.0000 between calls and the store held the right row -- the failure was not similarity and not storage

3_the_receipt_was_a_command_that_does_no.code: _recipe_of: env = ComputerEnv(); program_actions(..., target=target)   # no goal
3_the_receipt_was_a_command_that_does_no.why_fatal: a goal learned as `sort --unique {input}` re-derived plain `sort {input}` and reported THAT as the winning command
3_the_receipt_was_a_command_that_does_no.measured: PASS__RECALLED_AND_REVERIFIED with verify=DEDUPLICATED_SET_OF_INPUT_LINES while argv was ['sort','{input}'], and `sort` alone leaves `apple` twice in the file. The pass was genuine; the receipt could not do the job it claimed.
3_the_receipt_was_a_command_that_does_no.why_this_is_the_worst_of_the_three: the recipe is the only part of this system that leaves the sandbox. A wrong recipe is a wrong answer in the only form a caller can run.

three_defects_that_made_recall_impossibl.the_pattern: all three are the same mistake: a parameter (goal, seed_file) added to one call site and not followed to the others. This was the third, second and fourth instance of it in two rounds.
three_defects_that_made_recall_impossibl.the_discipline_that_should_have_caught_i: after changing a function's signature, grep every call site and assert on each one. I added the parameter, ran the new path, saw a pass, and did not check the call sites that produce the RECEIPT.

three_separate_processes_sharing_one_sto.speedup: 13x to 45x, and the command handed back is the one that actually works

measured_after.same_program_different_jobs: sort and deduplicate both use `sort` and get DIFFERENT argv, chosen by checking bytes rather than by position or by a table

a_false_alarm_i_raised_and_then_killed.what_i_reported: reverse regressed to OPEN__EFFECT_NOT_VERIFIED with rejected=['run_xargs'], FileNotFoundError '/tmp...'
a_false_alarm_i_raised_and_then_killed.what_was_actually_true: my fixture /tmp/perm/list.txt had never been created. The FileNotFoundError was the fixture, and the xargs rejection message was masking it.
a_false_alarm_i_raised_and_then_killed.how_i_found_it: re-ran ComputerEnv(seed_file='/tmp/perm/list.txt') directly and read the traceback instead of the status string
a_false_alarm_i_raised_and_then_killed.result_after_fixing_the_fixture: reverse closed in 0.65 s and recalled in 0.03 s. It was never broken.
a_false_alarm_i_raised_and_then_killed.the_law_reinforced: an instrument that reports a failure must be audited before the failure is believed -- including when the instrument is my own test script

what_they_pin: the second call is a RECALL, not a search
the recalled receipt carries the flag that does the job
a recalled recipe is still checked against real bytes
one program, two jobs, must not use one argv for both
tests_added.isolation_note: each test gets its own store, because a shared store made test #1's 'first' call a recall of test #4's result -- measured, and a test whose result depends on run order is not a test
tests_added.result: 4 passed, stable across three runs and inside a wider suite (23 passed)

regression.the_3: the R148 curriculum/boundary contradiction. test_the_first_time_learns_and_the_second_does_not asserts on curriculum_v1.study(), which _try_explore refuses before discover() is ever reached -- it has nothing to do with memory and this round does not touch it.

what_is_now_real_that_was_not: the permanence claim has a transcript in three processes with receipts. Before this round the machine was fast the second time and had learned nothing -- the speed was the fingerprint cache, not memory of the command.
sentience: no. Delete the store and only the commands are lost.
